extracted.intended_audience: EPA communicators, originators, designers, and publishing staff preparing EPA public information materials
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and production guidelines for graphic elements, file preparation, printing, paper, photography, figures/tables, and front/back matter of EPA public information materials. Covers technical prepress requirements, review/approval rules, and ecological/cost considerations for print and electronic deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize effective communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Design and graphic decisions must serve the communication goal — design is communication, not decoration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graphic design should work together with text to complement or supplement the message; aesthetics are secondary to communicating the message clearly and efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance efficiency, quality, and ecology
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphic and production choices should consider efficiency/cost-efficiency, best professional practices, and ecological soundness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow EPA Administrative Orders and GPO rules where applicable; because budgets are limited, cost-effectiveness is high priority while maintaining professional quality and sustainable production practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of color should be content-driven
rubrics_metrics.description: Use color only when it promotes effective communication (clarity, identification, or to reach an audience unlikely to seek out the information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid color for purely cosmetic reasons if it increases cost. For large-quantity press runs, color raises costs significantly; one color often suffices when content is easily sought/read. Two or more colors appropriate for public health/consumer issues or where needed for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color-count and approval rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Black (or blue) counts as a color; a two-color job is black plus one other color and not two colors in addition to black.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than two ink colors are required on a page, submit a written justification to the Agency Printing Officer citing applicable GPO criteria; local Printing Control Officers can approve two-color use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify use of more than two colors
rubrics_metrics.description: More-than-two-color printing requires written justification and approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for >2 colors must include a justification e-mailed, with PDF, to the Agency Printing Officer well in advance of printing; cite clarity, object identification, or other necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee photograph usage restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs of EPA staff may be reproduced only when they relate to public business, are necessary to explain the text, do not aggrandize individuals, are in good taste, are minimum size necessary, and show employees engaged in official duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid mug shots of executives/managers unless publication purpose is to highlight employees (e.g., awards program). Contractors and grantees should follow same rules when furnishing findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustration and photography best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrations/photos should be simple, uncluttered, and appropriate to the message; photographs of people often look best printed in black for one- or two-color jobs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With multi-color printing, specify colors as proportions of process inks (CMYK) rather than many Pantone spot colors; keep illustrations uncluttered and cropped to eliminate insignificant details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred platforms for electronic-design files
rubrics_metrics.description: Files should be created on Macintosh OS (10.2 or later) or Windows (2000/XP), with Macintosh preferred by the printing industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the Macintosh platform often reduces output problems and costs, though either platform is acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted desktop publishing software
rubrics_metrics.description: Use industry-standard EDPP applications for page layout, illustration, and image manipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended software includes Adobe InDesign, QuarkXPress, FrameMaker for page layout; Illustrator/FreeHand/Corel Draw for drawing; Photoshop/Corel PhotoPaint for image editing. Files produced in non-EDPP programs are more likely to have problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide native files and press-optimized PDFs
rubrics_metrics.description: Furnish native application files and/or press-optimized PDFs that include embedded fonts, graphics, color data, and layout structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PDFs for press output must be created using Acrobat Distiller with correct settings (not PDFWriter). Online/web-optimized PDFs are not suitable for press. Include native files whenever possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF and PostScript quality requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: PDFs must contain embedded fonts, graphics, color data, and layout structure; PostScript files may contain driver-specific limitations and are often not preferred by GPO vendors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PDFs created for web use might not output well for print due to resolution and color issues. If PostScript files are submitted, EPA takes responsibility for any PostScript errors encountered during output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliverable format guidance (HTML vs PDF)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose deliverable format based on intended use: HTML for searchable/online pages with limited layout fidelity; PDFs for online presentation and reprinting (press-optimized for future printing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press PDF maintains layout and should be requested for later printing; online PDF is for screen viewing and office printing only and not for press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font handling standards
rubrics_metrics.description: PostScript Type 1 fonts are the industry standard; provide the entire font set used; do not mix font types without care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide Mac printer and screen fonts or Windows .pfm and .pfb files. Converting type to outlines prevents font problems but makes text difficult to edit. TrueType and OpenType may be used, but vendors prefer PostScript fonts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color file preparation: CMYK and spot colors
rubrics_metrics.description: Files requiring four-color process separations must be submitted in CMYK; spot colors should be defined by proper Pantone numbers and identified as spot colors for output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit RGB files for commercial printing. Expect color shift when converting RGB to CMYK. Use uncoated Pantone numbers (EPA uses uncoated paper); specify uncoated (e.g., 462U vs 462C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Color-visual proofs limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Color visuals produced on office printers are not a reliable representation of final press output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digital and desktop printers produce different colors from traditional press inks; request contract color proofs to reveal color-shift problems; printed product on recycled paper may differ from proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scanning resolution requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Scan photographs at 300 ppi at input-to-output size 1:1; scan line art as bitmaps at 800–1200 ppi (1:1 ratio).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Save scanned images as uncompressed TIFF or EPS. For enlargements, proportionally increase scan resolution (e.g., to print 6x10 from 3x5, scan at 600 ppi). Crop/rotate/scale images prior to placement and work in layers when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital camera image handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid built-in camera compression; save camera images as TIFF before editing and submitting for printing; be aware of RGB-to-CMYK color shifts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If compression is necessary, use the lowest (highest quality) compression. Request contract color proofs to detect color shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking placed files properly
rubrics_metrics.description: All graphic files must be properly linked in layout software (use Place in InDesign); do not cut-and-paste graphics between programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cutting/pasting images (especially from Word/PowerPoint/Excel) can cause color shifts and crashes. If placed files are modified after placement, relink/update them before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofing electronic files
rubrics_metrics.description: Desktop outputs are guides, not acceptable proofs; always obtain appropriate proofs for electronic-file jobs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Print vendors are not obligated to match furnished visuals; request pre-production/blueline proofs for black-and-white and color-match proofs for color outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid extraneous/non-printing files on production disks
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include non-imaging or position-only files on production disks unless marked DO NOT PRINT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-printing images can cause confusion or file failures; clearly indicate any non-printing items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gradient creation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Create gradients to avoid banding; for offset printing use ranges of 3–97% and avoid 0% and 100% end points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digital printing may require higher highlight percentages. Proper creation reduces banding in high-res output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tint screen recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use tint screens under 5% (fine-detail screens disappear at high resolution); start at 10% and increase in 10% increments; avoid >90% screens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screens that look acceptable on desktop printers may disappear at higher resolutions; use conservative tint percentages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule (line) minimum thickness
rubrics_metrics.description: Never use rules (lines) less than 0.5 point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hairline rules may appear acceptable on desktop printers but vanish at higher print resolutions; ensure lines are reproducible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bleed requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide bleeds for any image that extends to the final printed edge; allow a minimum 1/8 inch bleed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originator must include bleeds in all files that image off the final printed page.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA paper stock environmental standard
rubrics_metrics.description: All EPA printed paper products must meet the New Environmental Standards: use 100% recycled paper with minimum 50% post-consumer fiber, processed chlorine-free, and vegetable-based inks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA documents must display the recycled logo and a statement indicating recycled content, processed chlorine free, and use of vegetable-based ink. Litho-coated, matte-coated, and dull-coated stocks are unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper savings and standard sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use paper-saving practices: single-space copy, duplex printing, combine tables/figures with text, crop figures; follow Joint Committee on Printing standard sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended standard sizes include 17x11, 8.5x11, 5.5x8.5, and 8x3-5/8. Use sizes to minimize waste and cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government bankcard printing restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of government bankcard for printing/photocopying is prohibited unless a waiver is approved by local Photocopying/Printing Manager or Printing Control Officer; Title 44 USC Section 501 limits sole-source procurements to $1,000 or less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver requests must include number of pages/copies, estimated cost from outside vendor, and required schedule. Journal page charges require EPA Form 1900-8 where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-house copy center duplication thresholds (JCP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Producing less than 5,000 units of a single page or less than 25,000 units aggregate (multiple pages) is not considered printing for black-and-white copying; color copying max aggregate is 100 units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jobs exceeding these thresholds must be procured through GPO (Government Printing Office).

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer and administrative review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All EPA communication products issued in the name of the Agency must undergo peer and administrative review and clearance before publication and external distribution, per EPA Order 2200.4A and JCP rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated officials must certify adequate review. The review process applies to EPA employees, contractors, and others publishing on behalf of EPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anchor elements required on public documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain anchor elements are required on all public distribution documents (publications using self-covers must include listed anchor elements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the attached anchor-elements PDF/templates and GPO templates; cover design should consider purpose and appearance, and follow physical specifications dictated by product size and audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page and front-matter formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Center everything on the title page using initial caps only; include peer-review notice/disclaimer/copyright on page ii; include foreword as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title capitalization: initial caps only (e.g., Handbook, not HANDBOOK). Place notices on page ii. Foreword usually provided by sponsoring lab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract types and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Use indicative (descriptive) or informative abstracts; limit abstracts to 200 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informative abstracts should report hypothesis, methods, results, and conclusions. For extramural and in-house reports include project/grant and date information as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of contents and lists formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin table of contents on a right-hand odd page; include front matter, main headings, appendices; include list of figures/tables only if helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dotted leaders, indent subheadings, avoid extra spacing that causes content to overrun; combine short lists of figures/tables on one page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acronyms, abbreviations, and symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Assemble and define acronyms, symbols, and abbreviations if it aids the reader; use parentheses after first use and then the abbreviation thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use two columns when the list exceeds one page. Define uncommon or specialized terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgments constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit acknowledgments to peer reviewers and organizations that aided development in a major way; do not mention EPA employees by name; mention of contract employees is generally not appropriate except for specific work attribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep acknowledgments concise and limited to those who materially contributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures: necessity and consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Use figures only if they relate directly to the subject and are necessary to explain the text; treat figures consistently throughout the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure line weights and shading are consistent; line weights must be >0.25 point; avoid tiny details that will fill or bleed; reduce oversized figures; ensure callouts are legible and high-contrast; no hand-lettered graphics; crop or mask photos to remove insignificant details; avoid border frames; place callouts horizontally and unboxed near items identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures numbering and captions
rubrics_metrics.description: Number figures consecutively using chapter number or appendix letter as prefix; put caption under each figure flush left following the figure number; capitalize only the first letter of first word and proper nouns; end with a period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start figures in each chapter with 1 (e.g., 1-5). Ensure illustrations are 300 DPI. Do not use footnotes inside figures; include such material in the caption or text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables: simplicity and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize tables for easy reading, use consistent format, and avoid overly complex stacked headings; center columns under headings and align on decimal; leave space between horizontal entries and avoid vertical lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number tables using chapter prefix; place caption flush left above each table after the table number; capitalize first letter of each word except articles/conjunctions/prepositions; do not use a closing period. For long tables continued on multiple pages, repeat 'Table X. Continued' and repeat column headings with rules on each page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table footnote symbols and order
rubrics_metrics.description: Use superscript lowercase letters for footnotes starting at top-left and proceeding left-to-right; for mathematical or chemical tables use symbols instead of letters to avoid confusion with exponents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use symbol order: * (asterisk), dagger, double dagger, section mark, # (number sign).

rubrics_metrics.name: References formatting and inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference sources for significant/original statements, information unfamiliar to readers, controversial matter, and opposing views; present references uniformly at chapter end or final chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use either number system or author-year system consistently. Include author(s)/organization, title, source, identifiers, publisher, place, date, and pages. Personal communications should be cited in-text only with permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices, glossary, bibliography, index guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Start appendices on the next available page; divide as A, B, etc.; list appendices in TOC; include glossary only if helpful; include bibliography for supplementary but uncited literature; an index enhances value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat each appendix title as a dropped chapter head. For glossary and index, consult standard style manuals for indexing instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research report structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Research (investigative) reports should present results/conclusions and supporting evidence; standard structure: Introduction; Conclusions; Recommendations; Methods and materials; Results and discussion; References.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place conclusions and recommendations early for reader access. Methods/results/discussion may be interwoven. Use explanatory copy and avoid large volumes of unedited backup data; reference background materials instead of printing them verbatim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project reports and manuals guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Project reports document research when a journal article or research report is not produced; manuals/handbooks/user guides should use straightforward, precise language and employ tables/graphics as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project reports are required in certain circumstances (e.g., when a journal article/research report is incomplete). Tailor organization and presentation to intended audience and technical needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: EDPP vs high-resolution PDF for press jobs
rubrics_metrics.description: High-resolution, press-optimized PDFs can replace EDPP files for printing if created properly (embedded fonts, graphics, color data, layout structure) but must be produced with Acrobat Distiller settings appropriate for press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PDFWriter-created PDFs are unacceptable for print. Use EDPP-native files when feasible; if providing non-EDPP-originated files, include press-quality PDFs and native files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized printers and printing procurement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain organizations are authorized to print EPA publications (in-house for <60,000 impressions single-color, GPO for most print jobs); contractors may not provide printing services under contract (duplicating for drafts allowed within limits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether GPO or in-house can meet schedule; contractor printing not permitted for final public distribution. Follow Printing Management Circular 94-1 and related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document preparation guidance for printing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use professional page-layout programs for multi-color printing; single-color jobs may be printed from camera copy; documents created in word processing software often result in lower-quality output for multi-color print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For 2+ color jobs, create files in EDPP applications; if not, supply press-optimized PDFs and native files. Provide clear instructions and output proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing information for cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: When requesting a printing cost estimate, provide number of pages, quantity, camera copy or electronic files, and any special requirements (color processing, shrink wrap, three-hole punch, rush delivery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For CD-ROM duplication include quantity, disk label requirements, size of files, shrink wrap needs, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required printing forms and deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain forms and deliverables are required for printing from camera copy or electronic files (e.g., EPA Form 2200-9; GPO Form 3868; GPO Form 952; CD with files; two laser visual copies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than two colors of ink are used, include e-mail approval from the Agency Printing Officer. Provide all fonts, graphics, printouts, folding dummy, written instructions, and GPO Disk Information Form 952.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal article page charges and reprints policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Page charges for journal articles and reprints are allowed under conditions; reprints of government employees' official work are procurement of government printing and must follow JCP requirements or waivers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page charges range widely; forms (EPA Form 1900-8 and journal order form) and approvals required. Articles printed in >2 colors need Agency Printing Officer approval. OGC guidance affects reprinting of journal-published articles; options include printing edited manuscript in EPA format with citation or printing through GPO with copyright release.

rubrics_metrics.name: When copy-center work becomes printing
rubrics_metrics.description: A job becomes 'printing' (must go to GPO) if it requires >5,000 impressions of any one page or >25,000 impressions aggregate as determined by JCP rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate impressions by pages x copies to determine if GPO procurement is required. Contractors may not be prime printers for reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and approval points for printing questions
rubrics_metrics.description: For price estimates and approvals contact the Agency Printing Officer (Washington, D.C.) or local Printing Control Officers in regions and labs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local PCOs approve two-color use and waivers for bankcard purchases and coated paper; Agency Printing Officer must approve >2 color use and certain reprint/color page charge requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top production checklist for high-quality printed documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow key practices: decide document type, use professional page-layout programs, use printing inks (not RGB), supply vector graphics as EPS, use TIFF for bitmaps at 300 DPI, use PostScript or TrueType fonts (prefer PostScript), print visuals on PostScript printers, produce color splits and visuals for contractor checks, and send all required files and instructions to Printing Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The stylebook lists software, file formats, printouts, color splits, folding dummy, written instructions, and form GPO 952 as items to send to local EPA Printing Office.
